prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished high-fidelity mobile navigation app design presentation for the real app "NavSkin", in Brazilian Portuguese. A premium, contemporary, carefully aligned, genuinely usable interface, influenced by the clarity and navigation hierarchy of Apple Maps and Waze without copying their branding. Landscape 3:2 image, TWO tall flat mobile screen mockups side by side at large scale, each approximately 393x852 aspect. No photographed devices, hands, perspective mockups or decoration. Thin neutral screen edge, subtle corner radius, generous but restrained outside margin, small editorial title above and tiny labels under screens. Screens should fill most of the image. Extremely crisp UI, impeccable typography and visual alignment, not a wireframe.
Preserve the app's distinct GTA San Andreas map identity: tilted dense city blocks inspired by Goiânia, BLACK thick roads, mid gray parcels, OFF-WHITE dense individual building footprints, deep green parks, pale blue water; small colorful game radar POI sprites with dark outlines, white bold condensed Pricedown-like place lettering with fine black outline, legible road names "AV. UNIVERSITÁRIA", "RUA 235", "RUA 227", "PRAÇA UNIVERSITÁRIA". Map is a real street network illustration, NOT satellite or a 3D videogame street scene. Use recognizable game-like condensed lettering for NavSkin brand and major labels, generously sized; numeric navigation information must remain highly legible and precisely aligned.
STRICT layout invariants from the user: map fills the screen edge to edge beneath UI. TOP has a very compact NavSkin wordmark block and adjacent separate theme/layers icon, filters/sliders icon, menu icon in one orderly horizontal row. No big brand card. Menu contains saved places/settings, no bottom settings button. BOTTOM has a restrained rounded search field with search icon and the exact placeholder "Para onde?". ABOVE the search field, a floating speed CIRCLE on the left with a large value and tiny "km/h", and a floating recenter CIRCLE on the right, ICON ONLY a target. No compass N or Rumo button. No visible attribution strip, no unlock/purchase bar. Controls have comfortable real tap targets of at least 44 points, most radius 14-20 except circular floating buttons. No glossy giant pill buttons, no arbitrary neon gradients, no oversized empty cards, no clutter.
LEFT screen is exploring: no route, map visible at least 78%, speed circle "0", search bottom. RIGHT screen is active navigation: a single compact prominent turn instruction card BELOW the top toolbar with bold right-turn arrow, "200 m" and "Av. Universitária"; a coherent cyan-blue route follows streets with one clear upcoming right turn; accurate white player navigation marker with black outline near lower center; small ETA strip at bottom above search with ONLY three aligned columns "12 min", "4,8 km", "18:42", each with tiny labels "Tempo", "Distância", "Chegada". Speed circle "38" and recenter float immediately above that strip. Enough open map between maneuver and bottom controls. Do not show GPS precision, additional speed inside ETA, traffic claims, real-time signal phases, or invented feature statuses.
All street geometry and route coordinates are illustrative prototype content. The image is a concept, not a screenshot of an implemented app.
Direction A, presentation title "01 / VIDRO". Small screen labels "Explorar" and "Navegar". Off-white studio canvas with very subtle cool-gray tone. UI surfaces are smoked/frosted translucent WHITE glass with carefully controlled opacity, slight map blur seen through material, fine white edge highlights and very soft realistic contact shadows. Graphite text. Elegant restrained cyan route accent. Turn distance and ETA typography highly legible. Quiet, tightly composed, premium modern navigation, no fake light blooms. Transparent surfaces must never compromise reading. SAME GTA map palette across both screens. Very refined glass, not silver chrome or liquid blobs.
